text:
maria: Heads-up — need quick takes on packaging tradeoffs for reserved capacity vs dynamic burst for the next pricing sprint. Primary ask: decide sequencing and minimal launch criteria so sales has something to pitch next week. TL;DR: customers want predictable latency and cost caps; finance wants clear commit paths.

kevin: For infra, reserved capacity gives the best latency guarantees. Dynamic burst is cheaper to operate but makes tail latency less predictable.

raj: Agreed. From finance POV: reserved -> predictable revenue. But we can model a hybrid: base reserved + burst credits. Need commit mins.

sarah: Sales reports three mid-market customers asking for an SLA and predictable unit-cost. They'd accept a 6–12mo commit. Also a few startups want flexible pay-as-you-go.

olivia: DevEx note — onboarding flows & SDK flags need to clearly show which endpoints are "reserved" vs "bursting" and how routing/fallback works. Docs + example config must exist at GA.

maria: Proposed minimal launch criteria: 1) tiered UI for reserve vs flex; 2) SLA language for reserved; 3) burst credits mechanic + UI; 4) telemetry for cost/latency per customer route. Thoughts?

kevin: Tech checklist: autoscaler behavior defined, fallback policies (model variant fallback), observable per-token latency. Also suggest a simple policy DSL:

```
route: app-x
policy:
  - reserved: 4xA100
  - burst: max_tokens_per_minute: 200k
  - fallback: gpt-compat-v1
```

kevin: If we ship without good KV cache metrics, cost complaints will spike. Need that for launch.

raj: Pricing ask — we should model three commitment bands (S,M,L) with burst credits that decay monthly. Finance will run scenarios if you give sample unit rates.

sarah: Can we give an interim sales play: offer 20% discount on a 6mo commit with 10% free burst credits month1? That helps close early pilots.

maria: Good. Need decision on sequencing: do we launch reserved-first (with basic burst) or launch flex-first and add reserved later? My leaning: reserved-first for enterprise sanity, then flex as self-serve.

olivia: Reserved-first adds onboarding friction (contracts, billing), but reduces churn risk for early enterprise customers. Self-serve flex is higher adoption but could abuse capacity.

kevin: Ops note: reserves require capacity reservations in scheduler which will change autoscaler policies. That's nontrivial but contained to infra. Flex-first avoids that but increases runtime complexity to enforce soft caps.

raj: Risk tolerance question: reserved-first = slower signups but cleaner revenue. Flex-first = faster growth, more churn, harder to forecast. Recommend reserved-first for next quarter launch.

maria: OK — provisional decision: reserved-first GA with basic burst credits and a roadmap doc to add richer flex self-serve in Q2. Action items:
- kevin: rough infra dev estimate + blockers by EOD
- raj: pricing bands + example unit rates by tomorrow
- olivia: doc/SDK surface for reserved vs burst by Thurs
- sarah: sales-ready playbook draft for pilots by Fri

launch-bot: Reminder: add "pricing-packaging" epic to roadmap and tag stakeholders.

maria: Thanks all — quick poll: :thumbsup: reserved-first, :thumbsdown: flex-first. Reply here.
